data.intent: Implement semantic GO task decomposition: preserve every numbered or bulleted request item as traceable task acceptance while allowing the agent to bundle coherent items or split independent work instead of blindly creating one task per number.

Release go-workflow-stack v0.3.6 so semantic GO intent decomposition and the corrected legacy contract migration are available through the installed Hermes runtime, with version alignment, regression proof, annotated tag, GitHub release readback, and local tool upgrade.

Fix installed stack-update source resolution

1. Honor GO_STACK when resolving immutable release tags from an installed go-workflow command.
2. Prevent site-packages from being treated as a Git checkout for stack update.
3. Add a regression test that updates a template through the installed-style runtime path.
4. Release and install the fix, then resume the blocked go-project-template pin.

Harden GO multi-item execution closure

1. Durably link the exact source instruction used to create a GO task, including a stable content hash and optional source reference for separate Telegram-message handoff.
2. Track every requested outcome R# as verified, blocked, or rejected with evidence.
3. Refuse manual and autonomous finish while any requested outcome lacks an explicit terminal disposition and evidence.
4. Add end-to-end regressions proving 7/8 outcomes blocks completion and 8/8 permits completion.

data.intent: Make completed task evidence audit-tight: bind a done task to its final commit, push target, and remote readback; make no_diff compare the claim base against the final committed tree instead of merely observing a clean worktree.
